open_obligations: Check how PR is computed and whether it is the same metric as Burns et al.'s PGR.
Check the strong-to-weak result where direct critique wins.
Check whether the gains hold across the full sweep of model sizes.
Check whether Wen et al.'s pipeline combines scalable oversight with weak-to-strong generalisation.
in.other_title: AI-AI: higher-order self-critique helps weak-to-strong supervision (PR scores)
in.rationale: Lang, Huang and Li, whose method is used to create a better weak supervisor to elicit the capabilities of strong models, ask which other combinations of scalable oversight and weak-to-strong generalisation work. Wen et al. report that when supervised models are larger than a fixed 7B critic, higher-order critiques generally give better PR scores than lower-order critiques, which they read as support for recursive self-critiquing as a scalable oversight approach where a weaker overseer supervises a stronger model. The passages do not show whether Wen et al.'s method is itself such a combination, so Wen et al.'s result does not answer Lang et al.'s question and neither bears on the other's claim; the link is navigation only until Wen et al.'s method is shown to combine scalable oversight with weak-to-strong generalisation.
in.scope: proposed SHARES_TOPIC: how a weaker supervisor can oversee a stronger model, which Lang et al. pursue by combining scalable oversight with weak-to-strong generalisation and Wen et al. by recursive self-critique
